question.text: Per Box 8.5 (GIPS-adapted guidance on appropriate benchmarks) referenced in Chapter 8 of the NISM XIX-E curriculum, which one of the following is NOT a stated characteristic of a valid benchmark for a Cat III AIF scheme?

answer.text: Guaranteed to outperform the fund's peer group over three years
Representative of current investment options and complete

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Box 8.5, a valid benchmark is: specified in advance, relevant, measurable, unambiguous, representative of current investment options, accountable, investable, and complete. A benchmark CANNOT be 'guaranteed to outperform the fund' — a benchmark is a NEUTRAL yardstick, not an alpha target. The fund either beats or lags it. The Trap: Options A, B, and D are directly from the Box 8.5 list. Option C is a trap — candidates may confuse benchmark with hurdle or absolute-return target. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C / XIX-D reproduce this GIPS-adapted list. XXI-B (PM) also tests it — the PMS benchmarking circular references the same characteristics. Manager's Pro-Tip: When presenting your Cat III benchmark to the IC, use the 8-point GIPS test as a checklist — if a proposed benchmark fails on 'investable' (e.g., the index contains unlisted names), or 'complete' (covers only 40% of your portfolio's strategy space), switch to a composite benchmark or a fixed-rate benchmark for absolute-return books.
